# pwtune

> pwtune measures any speaker with any microphone, builds a PipeWire filter-chain EQ profile from the result, and installs and removes profiles. A folder-scoped command-line tool for Linux.

Measure any speaker with any microphone, then build and install a PipeWire EQ profile from the result. The complete reference, for people and LLMs, is built into the tool: run `pwtune --llm`.
pwtune is one of the software projects by Jakob Hviid, all listed at https://jakob.hviid.phd/software/ (for LLMs: https://jakob.hviid.phd/llms.txt).

## What it does

- **Measure what a speaker does**: `pwtune measure` plays a logarithmic sine sweep out a speaker, records it back through a mic and prints the frequency response. It averages `--iterations` passes (3 by default) and changes nothing.
- **A starting EQ, written for you**: `pwtune create desk` measures, designs a parametric EQ toward a target curve and writes `./desk.draft.conf`. `--class`, from `laptop` to `fullrange`, declares how low the speaker may be pushed and adds a 4th-order high-pass at that corner.
- **Profiles that follow the device**: Each profile is a PipeWire filter-chain config that creates a virtual sink. Its `target-match` pattern is matched at install time against each sink, including a monitor's EDID name, so one profile follows the device across machines.
- **Made for scripts and agents**: Every verb takes a name and flags that answer its prompts, so the whole lifecycle can run non-interactively. `--quiet` and `NO_COLOR=1` keep the output clean, and `pwtune --llm` prints the whole guide.

## Install

Homebrew, on Linux. For x86_64 and arm64. On x86_64 it pours a prebuilt binary, so no compiler is needed. The tap is trusted once first, as Homebrew 6 and later ask.

```sh
brew trust --tap jakobhviid/tap
brew install jakobhviid/tap/pwtune
```

Or one line, without Homebrew. No compiler and no root: downloads the prebuilt binary for your architecture to `~/.local/bin` (set `PWTUNE_BIN_DIR` to choose another folder).

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jakobhviid/pwtune/main/install.sh | sh
```

Or build from source. Needs Rust. The binary lands in `./target/release/pwtune`.

```sh
cargo build --release
```

It needs PipeWire. pwtune uses PipeWire's `pactl`, `paplay` and `parecord`; PipeWire is the default audio server on most modern distros. Nothing else is needed: the sweep, the analysis and the EQ design are built into the binary.

```sh
```
